criteria.criterion: The reader brief for a retry (try again on <job>) and for a follow-up job that names an earlier job includes a section with the previous attempt's result (verdict, findings or outcome reason, end state) and the allowed change scope (deliverable paths and out-of-scope items), with the scope present even if the earlier reading had none.
criteria.evidence: briefs.rs prior_result_section covers earlier_attempt and referenced_jobs together. For each job it writes 'Job <id>: end state X; final verification verdict Y; N finding(s) or outcome reason(s) recorded.' It then lists the deliverables and out-of-scope items, or 'none recorded for it' with an instruction to state them. carry() in reading.rs fills end_state, verdict and reading_out_of_scope, and I traced the deliverable/out-of-scope split as correct. The findings themselves are still carried by the existing earlier-attempt section. The tests a_retry_brief_carries_the_previous_result_and_the_change_scope, the_scope_is_stated_for_a_retry_whose_earlier_job_had_no_reading, a_follow_up_brief_carries_the_result_and_scope_of_each_named_job and the CLI retry test assert this.

criteria.criterion: A new check function in athena-core refuses a reading for a retried or follow-up job that does not reflect the prior result or does not state the change scope, returning an error that names which of the two is missing. It does not apply to a first-attempt job.
criteria.evidence: check_prior_result_and_scope (reading.rs) is called in read_for on the earlier attempt plus the referenced jobs. It returns Ok when there are no earlier jobs. Its error says 'the previous result: it does not name job <id>…' and/or 'the change scope: it lists no deliverables/out_of_scope items'. A refusal reaches the user as reader_error. 'Reflects' is approximated by naming the job id (see findings).

criteria.criterion: The change summary or CHANGELOG states the root cause (the brief and the acceptance of a reading did not require the prior result and scope) and states the overlap with reading-omits-prior-verifier-finding-or-end-state: what it covers and what is left.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG Added entry says 'Root cause: the reader brief carried … but not where the job ended, its verdict, or its out-of-scope items, and nothing required the reading to use any of it'. The overlap paragraph says what is covered (the end-state half, the refusal check in code, and the prior-finding half only partly) and what is left (a check that each unmet criterion, blocker and major finding appears in the reading), and that the item is not edited.

criteria.criterion: New unit tests in crates/athena-context and crates/athena-core fail on the pre-change code and pass after. They cover the brief containing the result and scope, a reading missing the result refused, a reading missing the scope refused, a complete reading accepted, and a first attempt unaffected. Run `cargo test` and compare with the base.
criteria.evidence: All new tests pass. athena-context: 4 brief tests, including the first-attempt case. athena-core: carry_records_…, a_complete_reading_of_a_retry_is_accepted, a_reading_that_leaves_out_the_previous_result_is_refused, a_reading_that_leaves_out_the_change_scope_is_refused, a_reading_missing_both_names_both, a_follow_up_reading_must_name_every_job_it_follows, a_first_attempt_reading_is_not_checked and a_declined_reading_or_a_question_has_no_scope_to_check. They use PRIOR_RESULT_HEADING, check_prior_result_and_scope and the new EarlierAttempt fields, none of which exist in the base, so they cannot build or pass there. I did not run them against the base.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass from the repository root with no new warnings.
criteria.evidence: Athena recorded fmt, clippy (with -D warnings, so no warnings) and the full test suite (1454 tests) as passing on this tree.

findings.summary: Four changed files are outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: The deliverables list has only briefs.rs, reading.rs, run/mod.rs, CHANGELOG.md and config.rs. These four files were edited so the fake reader and the scripted test readers name the earlier job and give an out-of-scope item. Without that, the new check would refuse them. The edits are needed and small, but they were not planned. run/mod.rs and config.rs are listed but unchanged.

findings.summary: 'Reflects the previous result' is checked only by whether the reading names the earlier job's id
findings.evidence: A reading that contains the id but ignores every finding passes. The CHANGELOG says a per-finding check is still left, so the limitation is known, but the mechanism enforces only a proxy.

findings.summary: A refused reading is not re-read automatically
findings.evidence: The refusal is returned as reader_error with no reading, like any invalid output. The reading's assumptions said the reader would be asked again within the existing revision loop; in practice the user has to correct the reading and read again. The CHANGELOG states this behaviour.

summary: The change does what the request asks. For a retry and for each earlier job the request names by id, the reader brief now has a section "Previous result and change scope". It gives the end state, the verdict, the number of findings, the deliverables and the out-of-scope items. When the earlier job recorded no scope, the section says so and asks the reader to state one. A new function, check_prior_result_and_scope in athena-core reading.rs, runs in read_for after a reading is built. It refuses a reading that does not name each earlier job's id, or that lists no deliverable or no out-of-scope item, and the error names which of the two is missing. First attempts, declined readings and questions are not checked. The CHANGELOG names the root cause and says what the change covers of the queued item reading-omits-prior-verifier-finding-or-end-state and what it leaves. I ran the new tests: 8 in athena-core, 4 in athena-context and 1 end-to-end retry test in athena-cli, and all pass. They use symbols that only exist after the change, so they cannot build on the base. Athena's records show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. Findings are minor: four changed files outside the deliverables list (the fake reader and three test files, all needed so their scripted readers are not refused), and a check that tests only whether the job id is named.
